title: Introduction to AMRdb
text: package contains curated collection datasets designed support antimicrobial resistance (AMR) analysis across public clinical sources. focus primarily antibiograms_db, harmonized dataset integrating susceptibility profiles retrieved ENA, BV-BRC, NCBI, covering multiple bacterial genera. enables ---box exploration phenotypic resistance across antibiotics taxa serves robust alternative ad hoc clinical tables. Gene-level predictions also available via rgi_results, dataset produced using CARD-RGI annotations assigns ARO-based resistance features samples. genomic metadata allows comparative analyses phenotypic genotypic resistance trends. custom modeling validation workflows, AMRdb provides cleaned metadata test training subsets: training_db_cleaned test_db_cleaned include standardized MIC values, genus annotations, curated phenotype assignments preprocessing recategorization. corresponding raw metadata, stored training_metadata_db test_metadata_db, preserves original accession-level values annotations traceability auditing. Together, resources support reproducible classification, comparative genomics, resistance prediction pipelines user-friendly format.

previous_headings: STEP1 - Opcion A: Download data from URL
title: Download raw data from public sources
text: can download antibiogram files ENA browser, BV-BRC, NCBI using reference file available Zenodo, published July 4, 2025 (version 4). can compress file .gz format loading R. read_tsv() function supports reading .gz-compressed files directly. recommend simplifying column formats using janitor package standardizing column names shown .
code: # Define URL and local destination anti_url <- "https://zenodo.org/records/15809334/files/antibiograms.tsv.zip" # Replace "inst/extdata" with the actual path to your folder targetfile <- here("inst/extdata", "antibiograms.tsv.zip") # <- Change this to your own directory  # Download the compressed file download.file(url = anti_url, destfile = targetfile, mode = "wb")  # Unzip the .zip file unzip(targetfile, exdir = "inst/extdata")  # Import the data into R antibiograms_metadata <- readr::read_tsv(here("inst/extdata","antibiograms.tsv"))  # <- Specify the directory path # Compress the file to .gz format original_file <- here("inst/extdata", "antibiograms.tsv") gz_file <- here("inst/extdata", "antibiograms.tsv.gz") R.utils::gzip(original_file, destname = gz_file, overwrite = TRUE)  # Read the .tsv.gz file into R antibiograms_metadata <- readr::read_tsv(here("inst/extdata", "antibiograms.tsv.gz")) # Clean antibiogram metadata antibiograms_db <- antibiograms_metadata %>%   # Standardizes column names: converts them to lowercase,   # replaces spaces and special characters with underscores   janitor::clean_names() %>%   # Renames the columns   rename(     accession = reads,     scientific_name_Antibiogram = species   )

title: Curated Resource for Antimicrobial Resistance Data Exploration
text: goal AMRdb provide curated, high-quality dataset supports analysis, visualization, modeling antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Specifically, AMRdb enables researchers data scientists : Analyze outputs Machine Learning (ML) Deep Learning (DL) models, particularly related MIC (Minimum Inhibitory Concentration) predictions phenotypic classification (Resistant, Intermediate, Susceptible). Explore clinical genomic metadata associated microbial isolates. Integrate structured data reproducible workflows computational AMR surveillance comparative genomics.

title: Curated Resource for Antimicrobial Resistance Data Exploration
text: third dataset training_db_cleaned, contains curated preprocessed metadata CAMDA 2025 training set (training_metadata_db). Species-level annotations verified using Genome Taxonomy Database (GTDB), based Average Nucleotide Identity (ANI) calculated SRA accession. Two new columns added: scientific_name_new, corrected species name inferred GTDB new_genus, revised genus assignment, can used downstream steps reassess MIC interpretations. See ?training_db_cleaned full details. relevant variables standardized downstream analysis; see ?training_db_cleaned full details. fourth dataset test_db_cleaned, derived CAMDA 2025 test set (test_metadata_db).
